headline: Palo Alto Networks paid $500M for AI startup Console, sources say
summary: The cybersecurity giant acquired the two-year-old company, which automates IT help desk tasks with AI agents, for a significant sum in cash and stock.
details: Palo Alto Networks reportedly acquired Console, an AI startup specializing in automating routine IT help desk tasks, for $500 million in cash and stock. The companies officially announced the acquisition but did not disclose the financial terms.

Founded in 2024, Console had raised $29 million across two funding rounds, including a seed round led by Thrive Capital and a Series A co-led by DST Global and Thrive. Prior to the sale, Console was valued at $157 million, delivering a rapid return for its investors.

Palo Alto Networks plans to integrate Console's AI agentic functionality into its Cortex platform. This integration aims to enable security teams to investigate and resolve alerts using natural language, providing autonomous security outcomes across enterprises.

Console was founded by Andrei Serban, following the acquisition of his previous startup, Fuzzbuzz, by Rippling. The startup's customers included Ramp, Flock Safety, and Scale AI, automating tasks like password resets and access grants without human intervention.

The acquisition leaves Serval as a key player in automating IT service management among startups. Serval, a competitor to Console, achieved a $1 billion valuation after its $75 million Series B round last December.

This marks Palo Alto Networks' seventh acquisition in 2026, according to PitchBook. Other notable acquisitions this year include observability platform Chronosphere for $3.35 billion and cyber startup Koi for $400 million.

headline_marked: [[Delivery Hero board backs Uber's $15B takeover bid]], creating a global delivery giant
headline: Delivery Hero board backs Uber's $15B takeover bid, creating a global delivery giant
summary: The deal, valued at $15 billion, would significantly expand Uber's global footprint and position it as one of the largest on-demand food delivery platforms outside China.
details: Delivery Hero's supervisory and management boards have officially approved Uber's $15 billion takeover offer. They recommend shareholders greenlight the deal, which aims to forge one of the world's largest on-demand food delivery platforms.

The boards concluded the offer serves the best interests of the company, its shareholders, employees, and other stakeholders. They also deemed the price "fair and adequate" and anticipate accelerated product innovation.

If approved, the acquisition would double Uber's global presence in food delivery, strengthening its competitive stance against rivals like DoorDash and Just Eat Takeaway. Uber is already Delivery Hero's largest shareholder.
Uber has set a minimum acceptance threshold of 50% plus one share of Delivery Hero's outstanding capital. Major shareholder Prosus has also agreed to sell its 17% stake as part of the deal.

This move follows Delivery Hero's prior agreement to sell its businesses in 14 markets to SSW Partners for $1.6 billion. It also reflects a broader trend of consolidation in the on-demand delivery sector, with other recent major acquisitions.
caption:
Uber's $15 billion bid for Delivery Hero gets the green light from the board. This massive takeover could reshape the global food delivery landscape.

Delivery Hero's supervisory and management boards have officially approved Uber's $15 billion takeover offer. They recommend shareholders greenlight the deal, which aims to forge one of the world's largest on-demand food delivery platforms.

The boards concluded the offer serves the best interests of the company, its shareholders, employees, and other stakeholders. They also deemed the price "fair and adequate" and anticipate accelerated product innovation.

If approved, the acquisition would double Uber's global presence in food delivery, strengthening its competitive stance against rivals like DoorDash and Just Eat Takeaway. Uber is already Delivery Hero's largest shareholder.

Uber has set a minimum acceptance threshold of 50% plus one share of Delivery Hero's outstanding capital. Major shareholder Prosus has also agreed to sell its 17% stake as part of the deal.

This move follows Delivery Hero's prior agreement to sell its businesses in 14 markets to SSW Partners for $1.6 billion. It also reflects a broader trend of consolidation in the on-demand delivery sector, with other recent major acquisitions.
